scope: Try the provider-reported singleton enum/pattern workaround through a new exact provider-schema opt-in, preserving backend validation and all historical requests.
riskAnalysis: Schema constraint removal is safe only where the server-derived singleton already satisfies that exact pattern; exact enums and all internal identity/source checks remain. Preserve historical request hashes and consumed approvals. Live provider fix remains unproven.

threatModel.assets: Identity, source and evidence integrity; historical request and policy hashes; exact release/task approval; audit and financial uncertainty.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Provider-facing schema versus authoritative backend validation; new opt-in versus historical replay; request preparation versus execution authorization.
threatModel.abuseCases: Arbitrary pattern removal, wrong identity enums, changed historical receipt hashes, consumed grant reuse, reopening resolved targets and unsupported live-success claims.
threatModel.mitigations: Exact objective opt-in; ten server-derived singleton fields checked against original patterns; exact enums and internal validation retained; frozen historical requests; unchanged admission and permissions.

defects.rootCause: Support attributes empty incomplete responses to provider initialization of fixed enum plus redundant pattern; source contains the reported combination.
defects.detectionGap: Raw provider responses reported max_output_tokens and did not expose schema initialization details.
defects.regression: Provider schemas differ only by ten redundant identity patterns; internal validation rejects all ten substitutions; all five historical v1/v2 requests and policy descriptors reconstruct exactly; invalid singleton values fail before request construction.
defects.historicalPrevention: Attribute the finding to Support separately from observed raw failures. Preserve the old contract and receipts. Fixture success does not establish live compatibility.

defects.rootCause: The initial new marker was appended after the required report-profile suffix.
defects.detectionGap: Report opt-in requires the existing suffix to remain last.
defects.regression: The original five local failures were preserved; all 18 affected checks passed after inserting the marker before the suffix.
defects.historicalPrevention: Keep exact previous-objective aliases and verify full pipeline contract recognition when adding an opt-in.

rollback: Revert the new schema opt-in on feature Preview only; leave original receipts, old schemas/policies, revoked grants, accounting and Production intact.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Reject invalid singleton values before request construction and retain all response schema, evidence and source checks.
negativePaths.stale-state: Historical requests reconstruct byte-for-byte; historical policy evidence is readable but cannot pin current execution.
negativePaths.concurrency: No lease or concurrency code changes. Existing sequence and source-test workflow suites pass.
negativePaths.cancellation: Existing cancellation, lease expiry and authority revocation fixtures pass.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: Existing source-test workflow interruption and cleanup cases pass; no worker changes.
negativePaths.api-outage: Existing provider failure and diagnostic fixtures remain unchanged; no retries added.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: No task or grant is created by schema preparation. Resolved source targets remain inadmissible.
negativePaths.spending-limit: No model, counting, request, token, time or exposure limits changed. No paid request occurred.
negativePaths.partial-execution: Existing usage, failure evidence and shutdown handling retained; interruption fixtures pass.
negativePaths.duplicate-request: Historical approvals remain consumed or revoked; current policy selection rejects old policy pinning.

proactiveReview.architecture: Small versioned provider-schema change inside the existing implementation; no new adapter, controller, credential or orchestration.
proactiveReview.dependencies: Existing dedicated credentials preserved; no dependency changes or secret reads.
proactiveReview.threats: Arbitrary pattern removal, wrong identity enums, changed historical receipt hashes, consumed grant reuse, reopening resolved targets and unsupported live-success claims.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Schema equivalence cannot prove provider compatibility. Historical request reconstruction must remain exact. Resolved tasks must deny fresh admission.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Ten identity substitutions, invalid singleton, exact opt-in denial, frozen request/policy history, five-stage fixtures, cancellation and cleanup.
proactiveReview.independentChallenge: Independent Work QA and Auditor source review passed; final reviewed source and hosted verification remain required.
proactiveReview.recovery: Revert only the new opt-in; preserve original receipts, diagnostics and financial uncertainty. Never retry consumed paid requests.
proactiveReview.readiness: 16 final schema regressions, 18 prior contract checks, 61 combined workflow/review/bounded checks and 49 security/cleanup cases passed in overlapping groups. Live compatibility remains unproven; release qualification pending.
